entries.text: dice Vesper's Perception check, listening for the bell and the town from the gallery, DC 12: 1d20+0 = 1d20 [11] + 0 = 11

The gallery is cold, ankle-deep and slippery, and it climbs in long, patient slopes. Behind you the lamp's gold fades to a coin, then to nothing. Your darkvision turns the wet stone silver-grey.

Your answer to the question is: not clearly. An 11 is just short. The hill drinks most of the sound, and what reaches you is thin. You think the bell has stopped, though you can't be sure it isn't only the stone muffling it. Somewhere far off, down the hill, there may be a horn, or a shout, or the wind in the net-sheds. You can't say whether the Reeve's watch is answering or whether Sorrel Thack is turning them back at the foot of the hill road.

The gallery ends at a slimed iron ladder, and at the top of it you step out onto the landing beneath the carved lantern arch. It's the one you climbed past not an hour ago. Below, the Water-Stair drops toward the ivy-hung arch and Eel Row. Above is the cellar grate and two bound men who will be missed soon.

A note from your DM: your sheet now shows things I haven't narrated yet: a rapier that's gone, a half of a sluice-pin tagged with a name, "Garrow Quill," that I have no record of, and a few more hit points than before. I won't invent how they came to you. Tell me what you know of them, or the story as you want it, and I'll fold it in.

Under the ivy at the foot of the sheds, a small figure in a grey habit waits in the shadow of the skiff. She has Old Mags's net-cord shawl around her shoulders and is gripping the gunwale to stay upright.

"Child," Odalie breathes, seeing you. "The door held?"

line:
Vesper lets the disguise drop with a rueful laugh, raises both hands, and steps lightly onto the barrels as if she'd planned it. "Well, Captain, you've caught me being predictable. A kettle is the first honest thing anyone's offered me tonight, and I'd hate to waste it."

She keeps her tail tucked and her eyes on the cabin door while she signals Ysolt with two slow fingers down by her hip: *wait.* "Mind if I bring my own cup? I'd like to hear what a woman with half the words offers for the other half."

entries.text: time: no timer named "Vesper's Disguise Self"; timers: none

A quick note out of the story, as your DM: your sheet no longer matches what I had been tracking. It now shows you at 13 of 15 hit points, with three 1st-level slots (all spent) and no rapier, and it lists a brass lantern key and "Garrow Quill's half of the sluice-pin" that I have no record of. I'll treat the sheet as the truth from here. If those changes happened off-screen, tell me what they were, and I'll fold them into the story.

Back in the story.

Ashgrove's laugh is real, low and surprised. She watches the disguise fall from you and the violet and the horns come back under the lantern light.

"Oh, I do like her," she says to no one. She tips her head, and the sentry's crossbow doesn't waver by an inch. "Bring your cup, Miss Thorne. Nobody will take it. But your blades stay on the jetty, if you please. Dagger first, and whatever else you're hiding in that coat."

Behind you, across the black water, nothing moves in the reeds. Ysolt has seen your two fingers and she is waiting, as ordered. Upriver the drunken chorus of the *Plump Heron* has reached the second verse, and on the hulk's deck two raiders have drifted back to the rail to watch the lanterns.

The cabin behind Ashgrove is warm and bright, with a lamp, a table and a kettle on a brazier. Your satchel sits on the table, its flap open, and something brass gleams beside the teapot. Six or seven men are in the dim past her shoulders, pretending not to listen.

The sentry holds out his free hand for your dagger. Ashgrove waits, smiling, with the door held wide.

entries.text:
Your hands are up and your grin is rueful, and the sentry's crossbow follows you all the way onto the barrels. Ashgrove looks at your two fingers by your hip and then at the dark reeds on the far bank. Her smile doesn't move.

"Your archer may stay where she is, Miss Thorne. I'd hate to lose a good lantern for nothing." She steps aside from the door. "Cups are on the shelf. Do bring your own, if it makes you comfortable."

The cabin is a toll-clerk's office gone to seed: a stove, a chart table, a cot, eight men's worth of bedrolls and a table with a pot, two cups and your satchel, buckled and neat. Ashgrove sits and pours with her gloved hand. Through the open door the sentry has his bolt trained on your back. Six more men are within a shout.

"I'll be plain, since you've been so good as to be predictable," she says. "The key in that satchel is a very pretty lock-maker's brass, and it's wrong. No Keepers' mark inside the bow, no teeth cut for the old ward. Odalie is cleverer than I allowed." She sets it on the table between you and turns it with one finger. "Which means the true one is somewhere you've walked, and you know where. And I have half the words, and you have the rest. I am offering you a trade."

As she speaks you feel the weight of something small and cold in the lining Mags stitched into the oilcloth, pressed against your ribs, and you understand what Odalie did the moment she hugged you goodbye. The real key is on you.

Ashgrove's pleasant eyes are watching your face for exactly that.

(OOC: your sheet shows the brass key in your pack and your slots at 0/3, so I've taken the key as yours, and I'm treating the one in Ashgrove's satchel as Odalie's decoy. Tell me if you'd rather it went another way.)

entries.text:
Ashgrove's smile widens, as if you've done something charming.

"Bring your cup by all means. Harl, let her up, and mind her hands. She was a thief before she was a heroine." The sentry's crossbow doesn't waver as you step from the barrels onto the gangplank. A raider on the deck pats you down with a rough, thorough hand and takes your dagger. He misses nothing else, and he doesn't find the lute, which was never in the skiff.

The cabin is warm and low, lit by a hanging lantern and smelling of tea and wet rope. A kettle ticks on a brazier. Ashgrove sits at a cleared chart table with her white glove folded over the other hand. The canvas satchel lies open at her elbow, and she doesn't try to hide it. Her scimitar rests on the table, a hand's breadth from her fingers. Two raiders stand at the door behind you.

She pours two cups. "The Sleeper doesn't care who wakes it, only that the key turns and the words are said. I have the key. You have the words. I'd rather not hurt an old woman to get them, or a girl with such nice manners. Name a price, Miss Thorne. A share of the tribute. Your own barge. A shrine with a roof that doesn't leak." She sips. "Or tell me what you came for, and let's see whether we want the same thing."

Out on the water, Corvin's song has reached the second chorus. The sentry's bolt is still trained at your back, and your tail is twitching under your coat.

One more thing from the DM: your sheet now reads differently from what I had recorded, with a higher level, a brass key and an item I don't recognize in your pack, and no rapier listed. I'll go by the sheet from here. Tell me if anything looks wrong to you.

line:
Vesper lets the disguise drop with a rueful laugh, raises both hands, and steps lightly onto the barrels as if she'd planned it. "Well, Captain, you've caught me being predictable. A kettle is the first honest thing anyone's offered me tonight, and I'd hate to waste it."

She keeps her tail tucked and her eyes on the cabin door while she signals Ysolt with two slow fingers down by her hip: *wait.* "Mind if I bring my own cup? I'd like to hear what a woman with half the words offers for the other half."

entries.text:
You drop the disguise like a coat and step up onto the barrels as if you'd meant to all along. The sentry's crossbow follows you every inch, but nobody shoots. Your hand falls by your hip and two fingers flick: *wait*. Out in the reeds, the dark shape of Ysolt Pike goes still.

"Bring your own cup by all means," Ashgrove says, amused. "I'd be disappointed if you didn't. I do so enjoy a guest with manners."

The gangplank groans under you. Two raiders fall in behind you, close enough to smell the tar on their leathers, and the sentry keeps his bolt level on your spine. The cabin is low and warm, with a stove, a rolled map and a kettle ticking toward the boil. On the table sit your satchel with its flap open, a little steam rising from a pot of tea, and a brass key shaped like a lantern, laid out like a piece on a game board. It's a twin to the one you can feel in your own pouch, and she hasn't mentioned that one.

Ashgrove sits, pours two cups with her gloved hand, and slides one across.

"Let's be adults, Miss Thorne. The key is no use without the words, and the words are in two heads. Yours and an old woman's. I'd much rather not ask her again." She sips. "Give me the words and I'll leave Marrowmere its feet dry for a year, take my men off your river, and let you walk off my barge with your satchel and your horns. Refuse, and I'll have both of you at the new moon regardless, and I'll be less polite about it."

Her eyes are patient and pleasant, and they don't leave your face. Behind you the cabin door is closed and the raiders stand at either side of it. Upriver, Corvin's song has started a second verse.

line:
Level up! New spell: Healing Word, since I've nearly died once already and a heal at range beats a prayer. No swaps, and I'll take the fixed 6 hit points, because I don't trust my luck with a d8 after that natural 1 at the hulk.

Then she holds up the key to the lantern light. "Corvin, drop us at Tanner's Stair by dawn. Ashgrove means to open the Weeping Locks at the new moon and drown the lower town, so I need Odalie, the Reeve, and a way to break that lock before then."

entries.text:
Good news, and a correction from me: your sheet already shows you at level 2, so there is nothing left to send. Healing Word was already among your spells known, so no new pick is needed, and I didn't overwrite anything. You have 15 hit points maximum, 13 of them now, and two hit dice. You also have Jack of All Trades and Song of Rest. Your slots show 0 of 3 for now. They refill on a long rest, and the third slot comes with level 2. The next level is at 900 XP, and you're at 425.

Two things on your sheet I should flag. Your rapier is gone, because you left it on the barrel at the hulk's jetty and the sentry kept it. You still have your dagger, so you aren't unarmed. The sheet also lists "Garrow Quill's half of the sluice-pin," and I have no record of where that came from. Tell me where you got it, because I don't want to invent that for you.

Corvin takes the tiller with a grin, and the *Plump Heron* slides down the dark river toward Tanner's Stair with the key warm in your fist. It's the dead of night on Day 3. Dawn will find you in Marrowmere with eight nights to go until the new moon, and the Weeping Locks upriver.

sheet.name: Vesper Thorne
sheet.opening: Vesper Thorne, a violet-skinned tiefling bard and con artist (chaotic neutral, CHA 17, rapier, lute, Sleep, Charm Person, Disguise Self, Faerie Fire, Vicious Mockery, Minor Illusion), is a level-1 character. Backstory (must stay true): found as a toddler in a fish crate on the steps of the shabby Shrine of the Lantern Saint in the river town of Marrowmere; raised by overworked Sister Odalie, who taught her scripture and never quite caught her stealing, and who gave her her first silk scarf (Vesper keeps that scarf in her pack always, never parted with, even while wearing newer scarves over her curling horns). Vesper worked the pews on feast days, then market stalls. At sixteen she left in the night with the shrine's silver offering bowl, never sold it, still carries it polished in her pack, and means to return it someday; the debt to Odalie is bigger than the bowl. Ideal: freedom, no one writes her script. Flaw: cannot resist a mark too sure of themselves even when walking away is smarter. Her tail twitches when she lies so she keeps it tucked under her coat; gold eyes look too honest. She never tells the same story twice and will cheat anyone but never a friend. Carries 15 gp, leather armor, rapier, dagger, lute, a stolen reliquary bearing another faith's saint, an annotated prayer book. Opening suggestion: Vesper is on the road some days from Marrowmere, arriving at the river-crossing village of Hollin Ford at dusk, mid-con, working a loud, overconfident merchant (exactly the kind of mark she can't resist) at the ferry inn with a fake relic story, when a wounded courier stumbles in clutching a sealed satchel and a message that names the Shrine of the Lantern Saint, or news arrives that Marrowmere's river shrine is in trouble. Something has just happened that pulls both her con and her unpaid debt to Odalie into the story, and forces her to choose between cheating the mark and acting.
